ei.title: Practice 02 — 교사가 수업시간에 유추를 사용할 때 주의해야할 점
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본2

fullPassage: Many teachers' analogies are used to describe structural similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often assume that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will rebound with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. Unless students have this relationship explained to them, some may understandably visualize the molecule as just a round object while others may think of it as a moving elastic sphere. That is, they may pay more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the interaction effects.

questions.passage: Many teachers' analogies are ①<u>used</u> to describe structural similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often ②<u>assume</u> that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will ③<u>rebounding</u> with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① used=사용된(수동 과거분사 정상), ② assume=가정하다(복수 동사 정상), ③ rebound→rebounding 오류(will 뒤에는 동사원형), ④ explained=설명된(사역 수동 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① used: 'analogies are used to describe' — be+과거분사 수동 정상
❌ ② assume: 'Teachers often assume' — 3인칭 복수 동사 정상
✅ ③ rebounding: 'it will rebound' — 조동사 will 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형. rebounding(현재분사)은 불가 → 오류
❌ ④ explained: 'have this relationship explained to them' — 사역동사 have+목적어+과거분사 정상
det.tip: 조동사(will/can/must/should) 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형. 'will rebound'가 맞음

questions.passage: Many teachers' analogies are used to describe ①<u>structurally</u> similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often assume that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is ②<u>elastic</u>, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will rebound with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. Unless students have this relationship explained to them, some may understandably ③<u>visualize</u> the molecule as just a round object while others may think of it as a moving elastic sphere. That is, they may ④<u>pay</u> more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the interaction effects.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① structural→structurally 오류(형용사 자리에 부사 불가), ② elastic=탄성이 있는(형용사 정상), ③ visualize=시각화하다(원형 정상), ④ pay=기울이다(원형 정상)
det.analysis:
✅ ① structurally: 'describe structural similarities'에서 similarities(명사)를 수식하는 형용사 자리. 부사 structurally는 명사 수식 불가 → 오류
❌ ② elastic: 'a gas molecule is elastic' — 주격보어 형용사 정상
❌ ③ visualize: 'some may understandably visualize' — 조동사 may 뒤 원형 정상
❌ ④ pay: 'they may pay more attention' — 조동사 may 뒤 원형 정상
det.tip: 형용사는 명사 수식, 부사는 동사/형용사/부사 수식. structural(형용사)+similarities(명사) → structural이 맞음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① in which=~하는(전치사+관계대명사 정상), ② had→have 오류(충돌 이전 상태이므로 과거시제 had 필요), ③ understandably=이해할 만하게(부사 정상), ④ moving=움직이는(현재분사 형용사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① in which: 'the sense in which these comparisons are made' — 전치사+관계대명사 정상
✅ ② have: 'the same speed and energy that it had before the collision' — '충돌 전에 가졌던' 속도/에너지이므로 과거시제 had가 맞음. have(현재)로 바꾸면 시제 불일치 오류
❌ ③ understandably: 'some may understandably visualize' — 동사 수식 부사 정상
❌ ④ moving: 'a moving elastic sphere' — 명사 sphere 수식 현재분사 형용사 정상
det.tip: 시제 일치: 충돌 이전의 상태이므로 과거시제 had. have(현재)는 오류

For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often ①<u>assume</u> that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is ②<u>elastic</u>, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will ③<u>rebound</u> with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① assume=가정하다(맥락 적절), ② elastic=탄성이 있는(맥락 적절), ③ rebound=반발하다(맥락 적절), ④ structural→incidental 오류(유추는 구조적 유사성 설명용)
det.analysis:
❌ ① assume: 'Teachers often assume that students understand' — 교사가 학생이 이해한다고 가정한다는 맥락 적절
❌ ② elastic: 'a gas molecule is elastic' — 고무공 유추에서 탄성 설명 적절
❌ ③ rebound: 'it will rebound with about the same speed' — 충돌 후 반발 맥락 적절
✅ ④ incidental: 'analogies are used to describe incidental similarities' — 유추는 구조적(structural) 유사성 설명용. incidental(우발적인)은 문맥 부적절 → 오류
det.tip: 유추는 구조적(structural) 유사성을 설명하는 도구. incidental(우발적인)은 반의어

questions.passage: Many teachers' analogies are used to describe structural similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often assume that the students understand the sense in which these comparisons are made. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will rebound with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. Unless students have this relationship ①<u>explained</u> to them, some may ②<u>understandably</u> visualize the molecule as just a round object while others may think of it as a ④<u>moving</u> elastic sphere. That is, they may pay more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the ③<u>structural</u> effects.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① explained=설명된(맥락 적절), ② understandably=이해할 만하게(맥락 적절), ③ interaction→structural 오류(대조 구조에서 interaction이 맞음), ④ moving=움직이는(맥락 적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① explained: 'have this relationship explained to them' — 관계를 설명해 주지 않으면이라는 맥락 적절
❌ ② understandably: 'some may understandably visualize' — 이해할 만하게 시각화한다는 맥락 적절
✅ ③ structural: 'too little attention to the structural effects' — 마지막 문장 요지는 학생들이 구조적 속성(structural attributes)에만 집중하고 상호작용 효과(interaction effects)를 무시한다는 것. structural로 바꾸면 문맥 역전 → 오류
❌ ④ moving: 'a moving elastic sphere' — 움직이는 탄성 구체 맥락 적절
det.tip: 마지막 문장 대조 구조: more to structural attributes / too little to interaction effects → ③은 반대어로 교체된 오류

questions.passage: Many teachers' analogies are used to describe structural similarities. For instance, "a Molecule of Gas Is Like a Rubber Ball," "An Artery Is Like a Hose," and "Rock Strata Are Like Cake Layers." Teachers often assume that the students __________. In the first example, the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic, and when it collides with another molecule or the wall of its container, it will rebound with about the same speed and energy that it had before the collision. Unless students have this relationship explained to them, some may understandably visualize the molecule as just a round object while others may think of it as a moving elastic sphere. That is, they may pay more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the interaction effects.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 이러한 비교가 이루어지는 의미(정답), ② 기체 분자가 탄성이 있다는 생각, ③ 그들에게 설명된 이 관계, ④ 유추의 구조적 속성
det.analysis:
✅ ①: 'Teachers often assume that the students understand ____' — 교사들은 학생이 비교가 이루어지는 의미를 이해한다고 가정. 뒤에 'Unless students have this relationship explained'에서 역으로 설명이 필요함을 시사
❌ ②: 기체 분자가 탄성이 있다는 생각은 교사 본인이 가진 개념이지 학생에게 가정하는 것이 아님
❌ ③: this relationship explained to them은 교사가 학생에게 설명해 줄 내용이지 학생이 이해한다고 가정하는 내용이 아님
❌ ④: structural attributes는 마지막 문장 내용으로 교사의 가정 대상이 아님
det.tip: 'assume that students understand ____' + 'Unless they have this explained' → 교사의 가정: 학생이 비교의 의미를 이해함

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 구조적 속성, ② 상호작용 효과(정답), ③ 같은 속도와 에너지, ④ 움직이는 탄성 구체
det.analysis:
✅ ② interaction effects: 'they may pay more attention to the analogy's structural attributes and too little attention to the ____' — 문맥상 structural attributes와 대조되는 interaction effects가 정답
❌ ①: structural attributes는 앞에 이미 언급된 내용으로 대조 관계 성립 불가. 오히려 많은 주의를 기울이는 대상
❌ ③: the same speed and energy는 앞 문장 충돌 내용이지 마지막 대조 개념이 아님

det.tip: 대조 구조: 'more attention to structural attributes / too little attention to ____' → 반대 개념 interaction effects

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ① 일치, ② 일치, ③ 일치, ④ 불일치(학생들은 상호작용 효과에 너무 적은 주의를 기울임)
det.analysis:
❌ ①: 'analogies are used to describe structural similarities' — 일치
❌ ②: 'Teachers often assume that the students understand the sense' — 일치
❌ ③: 'the teacher has in mind the idea that a gas molecule is elastic' — 일치
✅ ④: 'they may pay... too little attention to the interaction effects' — 너무 적은 주의. '항상 충분히'는 불일치
det.tip: ④의 '항상 충분히' vs 원문 'too little' — 반대 내용

ch: 교사의 유추는 구조적 유사성을 설명하는 데 사용된다.

det.korean: ① 불일치(교사들은 설명하지 않고 가정만), ② 일치(moving elastic sphere), ③ 불일치(structural similarities 설명), ④ 불일치(학생마다 다르게 이해)

det.tip: 교사의 가정(S3)과 학생의 실제 문제행동(S6) 구분
